column2: but that code missed the case where the last event was at the

column1: very end of the page and has only 4 bytes left.
The checks to detect the corruption by the writer to reads needs to see the
length of the event. If the length in the first 4 bytes is zero then the
length is stored in the second 4 bytes. But if the writer is in the process
of updating that code
column2: there's a small window where the length in the first

column1: 4 bytes could be zero even though the length is only 4 bytes. That will
cause rb_event_length() to read the next 4 bytes which could happen to be off the
allocated page.

column2: fail immediately if the next event pointer is

column1: less than 8 bytes from the end of the commit (last byte of data)
